Foundations of Education

Education in nursing — philosophy, aims, the nurse educator’s role, and the nursing curriculum.

🎯 After this chapter you can

  • Describe the meaning and aims of education
  • Explain the nursing curriculum
  • Describe the role of the nurse educator
  • Explain curricula planning and evaluation

In simple words

Education is drawing out the best in a person through knowledge, skill and attitude change. For nurses, education is both a professional preparation and a service to patients and learners.

Aims of education

  • Intellectual growth — knowledge and reasoning
  • Psychomotor skill — safe procedures
  • Affective growth — values, attitudes and professionalism
  • Social growth — teamwork and communication
  • Professional growth — accountability and lifelong learning

Curriculum

The curriculum is the planned learning experience — objectives, content, teaching methods, and evaluation.

Curriculum element What it answers
Objectives What should the learner become?
Content What will be taught and learned?
Methods How will it be taught?
Evaluation How do we know learning happened?
Total experience Cocurricular and clinical learning

Curriculum types

  • Subject-centred — content leads the plan (most nursing curricula)
  • Learner-centred — needs of the learner lead the plan
  • Competency-based — safe, demonstrated skills define the outcome
  • Problem-based learning — real problems drive learning
  • Integrated — theory and clinical practice taught together

The nurse educator

  • Plans and delivers teaching in classroom and clinical area
  • Assesses student competence fairly
  • Models ethical and professional behaviour
  • Counsels and mentors students
  • Participates in curriculum and programme evaluation
  • Keeps own knowledge current through continuing education

🔴 Adult learning

Nursing students are adults. Andragogy (Knowles) says adults learn best when they know why the lesson matters, participate in planning and learn by solving real problems.

🔴 Most important for exams

  1. Curriculum = objectives, content, methods and evaluation together.
  2. Aims of education: knowledge, skill, attitude and professionalism.
  3. Competency-based education checks demonstrated safe practice.
  4. Knowles introduced andragogy — principles of adult learning.
  5. The nurse educator teaches, models, evaluates and mentors.

⭐ Important for exams

  1. INC sets the nursing curriculum and prescribes clinical hours.
  2. Problem-based learning improves critical thinking.
  3. Integrated teaching links theory with clinical practice.
  4. Lesson plans make teaching organised and measurable.
  5. Continuing education keeps competence current.

📌 Memory trick

Curriculum elements = O-C-M-E: Objectives, Content, Methods, Evaluation.

60-second revision

  • Education draws out knowledge, skill and attitude.
  • Curriculum: objectives, content, methods, evaluation.
  • Types: subject, learner, competency, problem-based, integrated.
  • Adults learn best when purpose is clear and problems are real.
  • The educator plans, teaches, assesses, models and mentors.

Test yourself

The four main curriculum elements are:

Answer: B. A curriculum is built from objectives, content, teaching methods and evaluation.

Knowles is known for teaching on:

Answer: B. Knowles is known for andragogy, the principles of adult learning.

Competency-based nursing education stresses:

Answer: B. Competency-based education requires demonstrated, safe and supervised performance, not only time spent.

Which curriculum is planned around real clinical problems?

Answer: B. Problem-based learning uses real clinical problems to drive knowledge and reasoning.

Who sets the nursing curriculum in India?

Answer: B. The INC sets standards of nursing education, including curriculum and clinical requirements.
